title: 4 months of building my typing game with the help of Opus 5.5 and my Product design experience. What was great and what was hard.
author: xcantene
selftext:
I'm a product designer and I wanted to make a fun, free game. I've always loved typing games, especially TypeRacer. I was addicted to it, and that's where all the inspiration came from.

The first challenge was how to make a typing game that wasn't a copy of the others. I've seen so many of them, from racing to spaceships. I wanted something where I also felt in control, with a bit of arcade and waves. After several rounds of iteration and design planning, I landed on this crazy idea where you decide what you want to type to defeat the mobs in each wave and reach the finish line.

It was challenging when I first tested it, because many people would always go for the simpler choice and win. So I spent a lot of time on balancing to make that choice actually matter.

I also wanted the game to be appealing beyond the visuals. I really love retro arcade games, so the music and the vibe were a big part of it. A large part of the art was done by me. Most of the flat art is vector images I drew in Adobe Illustrator and prepared in a simple way for animation.

The trick came later, when I started building tools with Opus, with Codex also involved. AI would often mess up certain areas, and I couldn't always fix them with normal prompts. So I made an animation studio for every character and mob, a simple low-poly 3D modeling tool for the assets, a synthesizer to create the sounds and music, and several tools for testing different game modes.

That was the big lesson for me. Instead of only asking the AI to get it right, I built tools so I could get my hands on the work and give it better input. My product design experience helped a lot there, because I knew when something felt wrong and could come up with a way to fix it.

This is the first large update and I still have so much more I want to work on. Next is the adventure mode, where you'll go on missions through different lands of the world, all by typing.

It's been a long road and a very fun project. If you want to try it, it's free in your browser, but you'll need a physical keyboard:

[https://typehunters.cloudwanderstudios.com/](https://typehunters.cloudwanderstudios.com/)

Have any of you built your own tools to work better with your AI agents? I'd love to hear what helped. If you tried my game please shoot me your feedback as well. I am always opened for suggestions and improvements!
